# phylogp

**Phylogenetic comparative models as Gaussian processes.**

`phylogp` fits models of continuous trait evolution as Gaussian
processes on a phylogeny. A model is a *kernel*, the covariance it
implies between species, and kernels are built by adding components:

``` r

library(phylogp)

k_bm() + k_white()                          # Brownian motion + residual (= Pagel's lambda)
k_ou(root = "fixed")                        # Ornstein-Uhlenbeck
k_relaxed() + k_white()                     # autocorrelated (relaxed) rates
k_rate_time(n_bins = 20) + k_white()        # rate as a smooth function of time
k_bm() + k_dist(geo_dist) + k_white()       # phylogeny + geography
k_bm() + k_slope("body") * k_bm() + k_white()   # slopes that evolve along the tree
k_bm() + k_white(df = 4)                    # Student-t residuals
k_edge("pow(len, kappa) .* exp(beta * he)", # your own branch-wise kernel
       pars = list(kappa = c(0, 1), beta = c(-5, 5)))
```

![Correlation between species implied by six kernels on the same
tree](reference/figures/README-gallery.png)

*The same tree seen through six kernels: Brownian motion, Pagel’s λ,
early burst, Ornstein–Uhlenbeck, relaxed rates and a squared-exponential
kernel.*

`phylogp` writes the Stan program for the kernel, compiles it once and
fits it with [cmdstanr](https://mc-stan.org/cmdstanr/), by maximum
likelihood or HMC. Whenever every component has the branch-wise form
(variance accumulated along edges), the likelihood is evaluated by the
O(N) pruning recursion and leave-one-out predictive densities by an O(N)
two-pass message passing; otherwise it falls back to dense algebra.

![True and estimated rates of evolution on a
tree](reference/figures/README-rates.png)

*A relaxed-rate kernel finds a clade evolving 8 times faster, without
being told where it is (from
[`vignette("phylogp")`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/articles/phylogp.md)).*

## Designing kernels

Before fitting, check what a kernel implies and whether it is valid on
your tree:

``` r

tr <- ape::rtree(50)                         # a tree with tips at different heights

kernel_check(k_dist(phi = "sqexp"), tr)      # squared exponential: can fail here
kernel_check(k_dist(phi = "exponential"), tr) # exponential (= OU): always valid

kernel_plot(k_ou(), tr, pars = list(ou1 = list(alpha = 3)))
kernel_equivalent(k_ou(root = "fixed"), k_eb(upper = 50), tr)  # same model at the tips?
y <- kernel_simulate(k_relaxed() + k_white(), tr)   # prior predictive draws
cat(make_stancode(k_bm() + k_white()))       # the generated Stan program
```

[`kernel_check()`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/kernel_check.md)
uses the theory first: branch-wise kernels are valid whenever their edge
variances are non-negative; on ultrametric trees any non-increasing
function of patristic distance is valid; on trees with fossil tips or
without a clock only completely monotone functions (such as the
exponential) are guaranteed. Where validity is not guaranteed it checks
numerically over a grid of parameter values.

## Fitting

``` r

fit <- phylo_gp(brain ~ body, data = d, tree = tr,
                kernel = k_relaxed() + k_white())
fit
loo(fit)                      # PSIS-LOO from exact conditional densities

loo_refit(fit)                # exact LOO for influential species
phylo_gp_trees(brain ~ body, d, trees, k_lambda())   # over a sample of trees
predict(fit, newdata = new)   # species without data (kriging on the tree)

ml <- phylo_gp(brain ~ body, data = d, tree = tr,
               kernel = k_lambda(), method = "optimize")
logLik(ml); AIC(ml)
```

Maximum-likelihood fits of the classical kernels (BM, Pagel’s lambda,
kappa, delta, early burst, OU with fixed or random root) reproduce
`phylolm` to numerical precision; this comparison is part of the test
suite.

## Installation

``` r

# fitting needs cmdstanr and CmdStan (install these first so the vignettes can run)
install.packages(c("remotes", "cmdstanr"),
                 repos = c("https://stan-dev.r-universe.dev", getOption("repos")))
cmdstanr::install_cmdstan()

# the package, with its vignettes (takes a few minutes: they fit Stan models)
remotes::install_github("ThomasPueschel/phylogp", build_vignettes = TRUE)
browseVignettes("phylogp")
```

For a quicker install without the vignettes, drop
`build_vignettes = TRUE`; the tutorials are also on the [package
website](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/articles/).

Kernel design tools
([`kernel_matrix()`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/kernel_matrix.md),
[`kernel_check()`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/kernel_check.md),
[`kernel_plot()`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/kernel_plot.md),
[`kernel_simulate()`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/kernel_simulate.md),
[`kernel_loglik()`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/kernel_loglik.md),
[`make_stancode()`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/make_stancode.md))
work without Stan.

## Learn more

- [`vignette("phylogp")`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/articles/phylogp.md):
  getting started, a complete analysis of simulated data with a
  fast-evolving clade.
- [`vignette("kernel-design")`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/articles/kernel-design.md):
  building your own kernels, checking that they are valid on your tree,
  and when two kernels are the same model.
- [`vignette("slopes-prediction")`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/articles/slopes-prediction.md):
  slopes that evolve along the tree, influential species, predicting
  species without data, ancestral states, and robust residuals.

## Status

Version 0.2.0. Planned: multivariate kernels and non-Gaussian traits.

## Citation

Püschel, T. A. Gaussian processes on phylogenies: a kernel framework for
building, checking and comparing models of trait evolution. In
preparation.

# Package index

## Fitting models

Fit a phylogenetic Gaussian process and compare models.

- [`phylo_gp()`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/phylo_gp.md)
  : Fit a phylogenetic Gaussian-process model
- [`phylo_gp_trees()`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/phylo_gp_trees.md)
  : Fit a model across a sample of trees
- [`loo(`*`<phylogp_fit>`*`)`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/loo.phylogp_fit.md)
  [`loo(`*`<phylogp_trees>`*`)`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/loo.phylogp_fit.md)
  : Leave-one-out cross-validation for a phylogenetic GP fit
- [`loo_refit()`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/loo_refit.md)
  : Exact leave-one-out for species with high Pareto k
- [`loo_group()`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/loo_group.md)
  : Leave-clade-out cross-validation
- [`stancode()`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/stancode.md)
  : Stan code of a fitted model

## Prediction and ancestral states

Predict species without data and reconstruct internal nodes.

- [`predict(`*`<phylogp_fit>`*`)`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/predict.phylogp_fit.md)
  : Predict trait values for species
- [`ancestral()`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/ancestral.md)
  : Ancestral states

## Classical kernels

Brownian motion, Pagel’s transformations, early burst,
Ornstein-Uhlenbeck and residual variance. Combine them with `+`.

- [`k_bm()`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/classical-kernels.md)
  [`k_lambda()`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/classical-kernels.md)
  [`k_kappa()`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/classical-kernels.md)
  [`k_delta()`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/classical-kernels.md)
  [`k_eb()`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/classical-kernels.md)
  [`k_ou()`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/classical-kernels.md)
  [`k_white()`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/classical-kernels.md)
  : Classical comparative-method kernels
- [`` `+`( ``*`<phylogp_kernel>`*`)`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/kernel-sum.md)
  [`` `+`( ``*`<phylogp_component>`*`)`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/kernel-sum.md)
  : Combine kernels

## Kernel extensions

Kernels for variable rates, distances and your own models.

- [`k_relaxed()`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/k_relaxed.md)
  : Relaxed (autocorrelated) rates
- [`k_rate_time()`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/k_rate_time.md)
  : Rate of evolution as a smooth function of time
- [`k_dist()`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/k_dist.md)
  : Distance-based kernels
- [`k_edge()`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/k_edge.md)
  : User-defined branch-wise kernels
- [`k_slope()`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/k_slope.md)
  : Phylogenetically varying slopes
- [`` `*`( ``*`<phylogp_scale>`*`)`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/kernel-product.md)
  [`` `*`( ``*`<phylogp_component>`*`)`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/kernel-product.md)
  [`` `*`( ``*`<phylogp_kernel>`*`)`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/kernel-product.md)
  : Multiply a kernel by a covariate

## Designing and checking kernels

Look at a kernel, simulate from it and check that it is valid on a tree.

- [`kernel_check()`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/kernel_check.md)
  : Check that a kernel is a valid covariance on a tree
- [`kernel_plot()`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/kernel_plot.md)
  : Plot the correlations implied by a kernel
- [`kernel_matrix()`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/kernel_matrix.md)
  : Covariance matrix implied by a kernel
- [`kernel_simulate()`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/kernel_simulate.md)
  : Simulate traits from a kernel
- [`kernel_loglik()`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/kernel_loglik.md)
  : Log-likelihood of a kernel in R
- [`kernel_equivalent()`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/kernel_equivalent.md)
  : Do two kernels imply the same distribution for the tips?

## Rates, slopes and tree plots

Summaries of estimated rates and slopes, and trees coloured by them.

- [`edge_rates()`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/edge_rates.md)
  : Branch rates from a relaxed-rate fit
- [`plot_edge_rates()`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/plot_edge_rates.md)
  : Plot branch rates on the tree
- [`plot_tree_rates()`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/plot_tree_rates.md)
  : Plot a tree with branches coloured by rate
- [`rate_through_time()`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/rate_through_time.md)
  : Rate of evolution through time
- [`varying_slopes()`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/varying_slopes.md)
  : Species- and node-level slopes from a varying-slope fit
- [`plot_tree_values()`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/plot_tree_values.md)
  : Plot a tree with branches coloured by a value

## Stan code and data

- [`make_stancode()`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/make_stancode.md)
  : Stan code for a kernel
- [`make_standata()`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/make_standata.md)
  : Data for the Stan program of a kernel
- [`tree_info()`](https://thomaspueschel.github.io/phylogp/reference/tree_info.md)
  : Pre-compute the tree quantities used by phylogp
